title: When is the motion due?
instructions: Civil Procedure • Apply fictional Practice Order 7. Work closed-book. Assume no holidays or closures.

questions.source: Practice Order 7 (fictional), § 1: Exclude the day notice is served. Count every following calendar day. If the last day is Saturday or Sunday, continue to the next Monday.
questions.explanation: Service starts the clock, but the day of service is excluded.

recall.prompt: What starts the clock, and how is that day counted?
recall.model: Service starts the clock. Exclude the day of service.

justification.prompt: Justify your choice in one sentence.
justification.model: Sunday is a weekend endpoint, so the order continues the deadline to Monday.

questions.text: Which method computes the nominal endpoint?
questions.source: Practice Order 7 (fictional), § 1: Exclude the day notice is served. Count every following calendar day. If the last day is Saturday or Sunday, continue to the next Monday.
questions.explanation: Begin on the day after service, counting calendar days.

recall.prompt: State the counting method before looking.
recall.model: Exclude service day and count each following calendar day.

choices.text: Start after service and count calendar days.
choices.why: This applies both parts of the counting method.

choices.text: Start on service and count calendar days.
choices.why: This includes the excluded trigger day.

choices.text: Start after service and count weekdays.
Start on service and count weekdays.
choices.why: This includes the trigger day and removes intervening weekends.

questions.source: Practice Order 7 (fictional), § 1: Exclude the day notice is served. Count every following calendar day. If the last day is Saturday or Sunday, continue to the next Monday.
questions.explanation: Friday is day one, Saturday day two, and Sunday day three. Move the endpoint to Monday.
questions.facts: Notice is served Thursday. Counsel has three days to file a motion.
questions.caseIdentification: Original hypothetical applying fictional Practice Order 7.

choices.why: Sunday is the nominal endpoint and requires an adjustment.
Monday is the first Monday after the nominal Sunday endpoint.
Tuesday follows only if both weekend days are incorrectly omitted.

questions.text: Notice is served Tuesday with two days to respond. Give the deadline and shift service by the fewest days forward that would make the deadline Monday.
questions.source: Practice Order 7 (fictional), § 1: Exclude the day notice is served. Count every following calendar day. If the last day is Saturday or Sunday, continue to the next Monday.
questions.explanation: Wednesday service still ends Friday. Thursday service produces a Saturday endpoint.

key.model: Originally Thursday. Move service forward two days to Thursday. The second day is Saturday, so the response is due Monday.

tomorrow.text: A four-day period starts with service on Friday. Reconstruct the count and give the deadline.
tomorrow.source: Practice Order 7 (fictional), § 1: Exclude the day notice is served. Count every following calendar day. If the last day is Saturday or Sunday, continue to the next Monday.
